title: 3 AM Customer
description:
Three in the morning on the night shift. Only the refrigerator compressor and fluorescent lights were making noise.

The door opened and a man in a low hat walked in. He circled the aisles, then placed two triangle kimbap and an energy drink on the counter.

As {name} scanned them, the hat shifted. His hand stopped over the receipt. He had seen that face on television more than once.

choices.text: Act like you don't recognize him
choices.result_text:
"Thank you." Even the voice was the one from TV.

The man left. The convenience store went quiet again.

{name} wiped down the counter. Like always.
Somehow comforting — this person eats triangle sandwiches at 3 AM too.

The man paused, then smiled.
"On my days off, I'm just a person."

On the way out, he signed the back of the receipt.

{name} put it in his wallet. Not selling it.

title: In the Waiting Room
description:
Sitting in the interview waiting area — the person next to {name} looked familiar.

A high school classmate. Different class, but the face was in the graduation photo.

They recognized {name} too.

Both here for the same company interview.

choices.result_text:
Waited together for 30 minutes before being called.
Old school memories surfaced. Even remembered a teacher's name.

Both got hired. First day, ran into each other in the hall.
"We're together again." Didn't feel awkward.

choices.text: Just nod and focus on preparation
choices.result_text:
The interview was individual.
{name} was called in first. Did well.

Coming out, the classmate's seat was empty.
No idea if they got in. No contact info either.

title: Life Advice from a Drunk
description:
Right before closing. A drunk man in his 40s walked in.

Paid for a can of beer and looked about to leave — then stopped at the counter.

"Got laid off at 40. Best thing that ever happened to me."

Empty convenience store. {name} pretended to wait for the next customer.

choices.result_text:
He talked for 20 minutes.
Got laid off, opened a chicken place that failed, started small logistics work.
"But it's all my story now. I can tell it like it's someone else's. That's when you know you made it."

He left. {name} turned that over in his head for a while.

choices.text: Ask sincerely — "How did you keep going?"
choices.result_text:
The man stopped. Looked at {name} properly for the first time.

"Keep going? No. I just got up the next day. Every day."

Finished the beer and stood up.
"You just get up too. Every day."

{name} thought about that while mopping up for closing.

title: Rejection, Then
description:
10 AM. A text arrived.

'Thank you for your application, however regrettably...'

{name} turned off the screen. Looked out the window.

30 seconds later, the phone rang. Unknown number.

choices.result_text:
A company {name} had applied to three months ago and given up on.
"We had a hiring freeze at the time, but a position opened. Still looking?"

{name} paused briefly.
"Yes. I am."

The rejection text was still on screen. Decided not to think about it.

Missed call notification remained.
Called back — they'd already reached another candidate.

{name} saved the number.
Decided to answer unknown numbers from now on.

title: Found a Wallet
description:
The evening crowd had thinned on the subway stairs. A black wallet lay open against the wall.

{name} passed it, then climbed back two steps. Inside were several cards, three 50,000-won bills, and a business card for a senior executive at ○○ Group.

An announcement repeated near the gates. People kept moving around the hand holding the wallet, and no one else stopped.

choices.text: Hand it in to station staff
choices.result_text:
A text came a week later. The number from the business card.
"Thank you for the other day. Can I buy you a meal?"

{name} stared at the screen for a long moment.
An unsaved number and a meeting place sat side by side on the display.

choices.text: Take the cash and leave the wallet
choices.result_text:
Three 50,000-won bills.

Station staff walked past. {name} went down the stairs.

Every step home felt heavy.
150,000 won gained, felt like nothing was gained.
This is what money weighs.

title: At the Register
description:
At a neighborhood convenience-store register, {name} set instant rice, eggs, and ramyeon on the counter and handed over his card.

'Credit limit exceeded.'

The clerk tried it again, and the corner of the next customer's basket tapped his calf. He scanned the price labels and reached for the first thing to put back.

"I'll pay."

The card of a woman in her 50s was already waiting beside the terminal.

choices.text: "Thank you. If you give me your account I'll send it right away"
choices.result_text:
She smiled.
"It's fine. I was there once too."

The transaction ended and they went separate ways.

{name} gathered the bag handles into one hand in the parking lot. The woman had already disappeared beyond the crosswalk.

choices.text: "It's okay" and put the items back
choices.result_text:
Walked out empty-handed. Sky was overcast.

Had to make it until next payday. Could manage it.
That was all that could be done right now.

title: The Interviewer's Offer
description:
The interview completely fell apart.

Answers tangled, rambled, and a 10-second silence on the final question.

The interviewer stopped shuffling papers.

"Not for our current opening, but — are you interested in a different position?"

choices.result_text:
Contract position. Lower terms than regular staff.
But potential for conversion after 6 months.

{name} accepted on the spot.

A failed interview opened a door. Just a different door.

choices.text: Politely decline. There's a specific role in mind
choices.result_text:
"Thank you, but I'm looking in a different direction."

The interviewer nodded. Handed over a business card.
"Call anytime if that changes."

{name} put the card in his wallet.

title: Used Goods Transaction
description:
Listed unused items on a secondhand app.

A buyer appeared. Meeting spot: in front of a café near Gangnam Station.

A man in his 50s arrived. Looked at the item, said "I'll use this well," paid the asking price.

"What are you up to these days?" he asked.

choices.result_text:
The man thought for a moment.
"I came up to Seoul at 33 too. Let's talk sometime."

Received his business card. Head of a small investment firm.

Sold an item for 30,000 won, got a contact.
Never knew used goods trading worked like this.

choices.text: "Just clearing things out" — keep it brief
choices.result_text:
He smiled and left.
30,000 won gained.

Just a transaction. That's all it was.

title: What a Customer Left Behind
description:
Closing cleanup on the night shift, after the last customer had left and the automatic door was locked.

While stacking chairs and wiping under a table, {name} found a black envelope. Inside was a rubber-banded stack of 50,000-won bills. Two counts gave the same total: 500,000 won.

The red light on the ceiling camera blinked. No one returned while he tied the trash bags.

choices.result_text:
Manager arrived 30 minutes later. Reached the customer.

The customer came, took the bag. Gave {name} 100,000 won.

"Thank you. That was everything I had."

That sentence stayed longer than the 100,000 won.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice and take it
choices.result_text:
Got home and took the bag out.
500,000 won.

Lay down to sleep. Couldn't sleep.
Thought about the CCTV. The customer might come back.

{name} stared at the ceiling all night.
This is what money weighs.

title: Resignation and Offer — Same Day
description:
Was planning to hand in the resignation today.

Writing the email on the morning commute.

Then a call came in. A company {name} had applied to a month ago.
"Can you start tomorrow?"

The train stopped. This was the station to get off at.

choices.result_text:
Got off the train.
Went to a café instead of the office.

Sent the resignation by email and ordered a coffee.

Forfeited a month's pay.
But today was the first time work felt worth looking forward to.

choices.text: "Can I have a week?" — wrap up the current job properly
choices.result_text:
The new company agreed.

Asked for a week for handover. The team lead was grateful.

Last day, coworkers brought a small cake.
There were hard times, but the cake is what's remembered.

title: News from Next Door
description:
{name} ran into the next-door neighbor in the goshiwon hallway. For six months, that neighbor had studied for the civil service exam, with lamplight leaking under the door every night.

Today there was no thick exam book in his hands. He kept waking his phone instead. His face looked sleepless, but the corners of his mouth would not stay down.

Before {name} could ask, he held out the screen.

"I passed."

choices.result_text:
"Really? Congratulations."

As he said it, {name} checked his own reaction.
There was envy. But the smile came first.

They stood in the narrow hall and opened the results page again. The name and candidate number were still there.

choices.text: Think quietly — "I need to get out of here too"
choices.result_text:
That night, {name} rewrote the plan.

Vague numbers became specific.
Seeing the person next door leave — this is what it's good for.

title: Scratch or Not
description:
A scratch ticket by the convenience store register.

A sticker read: "1st prize winner from this location today!"

{name} picked up a 5,000 won ticket.
That's 5,000 won out of this month's food budget.

choices.result_text: Paid and went outside to scratch it with a coin.

Put the ticket down.
Expected value — always a losing game.

Bought a triangle sandwich with 5,000 won instead. Felt full.
More reliable return on investment.

title: Scratch Result
description:
Sat on the bench outside and scratched.

First box: nothing.
Second box: nothing.
Third box —

choices.result_text:
50,000 won.

Not 1st or 2nd prize. But 50,000 won.

{name} didn't reinvest it or buy more tickets.
Just got a proper meal. Something good.

Whether that's the right use of a lottery win — unclear. But it felt good.
